title: Godot (game engine)
summary: Godot is an open-source game engine initially developed in Buenos Aires by Juan Linietsky and Ariel Manzur, released under the MIT License in 2014. It uses a node-scene hierarchy where nodes represent functional units connected by signals, organized into reusable, instantiable, and nestable scenes. All game resources, including scripts and assets, are stored as files to facilitate version control collaboration. The engine supports multiple scripting languages, primarily GDScript (a gradually typed, Python-like language), C#, and C++, with GDExtension enabling bindings to other languages. It enables 2D and 3D game development targeting desktop, mobile, web, console, and XR platforms without licensing fees, though popular consoles require third-party porting due to SDK incompatibility with its open-source license.

mechanisms.title: Node-Scene Hierarchy
mechanisms.explanation: Godot structures game objects as a hierarchy of nodes organized into scenes. Nodes can inherit behavior through class derivation and are connected by signals to transmit data objects. Scenes are reusable, instantiable, and nestable groups of nodes, forming the fundamental structure for game objects and levels.

mechanisms.title: File-Based Resource Storage
mechanisms.explanation: All game resources, including scripts and graphical assets, are saved as part of the computer's file system rather than in a database. This design is intended to facilitate collaboration between development teams using software version control systems.
